reason: Verified in the source, in the DOM and in the geometry. VIEW.quiet (lately.html ~line 749) prints the reassurance card and then calls strip() unmodified; strip() reads the single module-scope D, which is built from the one fixture before ?state= is ever parsed. Driven at file://.../lately.html?v=light&state=quiet&motion=settled, the quiet band renders "Nothing is sitting" / "All 9 open jobs has moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, and every one has a name on it" and directly beneath it a card headed "How long open work has been sitting", "OLDEST - 41 DAYS", nine dots of which three carry .old (19, 23 and 41 days), and a screen-reader line ending "3 jobs have been open longer than a fortnight." Measured, the gap between the two cards is exactly 0px and the pair spans 570px at 1440x960 and 643px at 390x844 - both inside one viewport, so the claim and its refutation are on screen together at every size, not merely near each other. The seat's "two centimetres lower" and "bottom edge touches" are literally right. Not already handled: nothing in lock.md or brief.md licenses the quiet state to run on the loud fixture, and the coverage line's lab-authored provenance note is a statement about where numbers came from, not permission for a sentence to contradict them. Not a gate restatement: interaction-check.mjs asserts marks-past-the-fortnight == status.sitting only for state=full (~line 330), and the quiet loop it does run only checks that the reading instant is stated once. Breaks no constraint - no colour, no weight, no new metric, no architecture change. SEVERITY CORRECTED, blocking -> misleading. The surface renders, every control works, the keyboard model is intact and the shared denominator holds; what fails is the truth of one sentence, which is the stated definition of misleading ("the product asserts something untrue") rather than blocking ("the product will not do what it says"). This changes nothing about whether the engagement can close - both classes gate - but the class should be right in the ledger. The seat's fix is directionally correct and I am confirming the finding on it, but it is wrong in three load-bearing places and must not be implemented as written; see sharpenedFix. Also worth recording: the same line carries a plain subject-verb disagreement, "All 9 open jobs HAS moved", which the panel should not have to find twice.
sharpenedFix: Keep "derive the sentence from the data the strip draws". Correct four things before building. (1) Do NOT fall back to movementTwo(). VIEW.quiet already composes movementOne() + its own band + movementThree(); rendering movementTwo() in the else branch makes ?state=quiet byte-identical to ?state=full, which is precisely the duplicate-frame defect this master's own URL-contract comment records as paid for (thirty-six of forty frames identical for nine rounds). Make disagreement structurally impossible instead: compute const q = { sitting, overdue, unowned, oldest } from the same accessor the strip reads, and let the quiet band's card be a function of q - reassurance when all three are 0 and every age < D.fortnight, otherwise the count it actually has, still in the quiet band's own layout. (2) A quiet fixture cannot be hand-edited: fixture.js is emitted by derive-fixture.mjs and `--check` exits 2 on drift. Add a second lab-authored set there (e.g. quiet: { jobs, status }) that keeps openCount at the bound activeRootTaskCount of 9 and still carries the three rootTaskTitles verbatim and in order, with all nine ages under 14 and sitting/overdue/unowned/waiting all 0. The seat's "Oldest - 11 days" is an instruction to the new fixture, not a reading of the current one - it is only true if the three re-aged jobs land at or below 11. (3) D must become state-aware, which it is not today: D is built at module scope (~line 466) and D.oldest, D.axisMax, D.sitting, D.overdue, D.unowned and D.peak are all derived there, while the ?state= parse does not run until ~line 830. Either move the URL contract above D or rebind D once the state is known - this is a small build, not the one-line edit the finding implies. (4) Do not hardcode "have". D.open is data, so "All 1 open job have moved" is the mirror of the bug being fixed the moment activeRootTaskCount is 1; select the verb from the same number, e.g. `All ${plural(D.open, "open job", "open jobs")} ${D.open === 1 ? "has" : "have"} moved inside a fortnight`. (5) Close it in the gate, not only in the fixture: extend interaction-check.mjs's marks-vs-claim assertion beyond state=full so that, in every state that renders strip(), no reassurance sentence may print while any dot carries .old, and the "Oldest - N days" head must be under D.fortnight whenever "Nothing is sitting" is on screen. Without that the same drift returns the next time a fixture moves.
breaks: A quiet fixture changes the quiet frames, so light-quiet--1440x960.png and its dark twin must be re-shot and frames.json regenerated. Nine ages all under 14 crowd every dot into the left ~30% of the strip, and the de-swarm packs at a 16px minimum, so it will stack more rows than the current spread: strip minHeight grows, the ages card gets taller, and dot hit targets and their tint contrast must be re-measured by audit.mjs at 390 as well as 1440. Making D state-aware is the wider risk - it touches every state, including the loading skeleton, which renders movementOne() + movementTwo() for its geometry; re-verify that full, partial, first-run, empty, loading and error frames are unchanged byte-for-byte afterwards, or the fix has quietly redesigned six states to repair one. Re-run in this order: `node derive-fixture.mjs --check` (the four bound facts and the jobs.length == openCount guard), interaction-check.mjs in full (Oldest label, dot count and .old count, tooltip pin/dismiss under touch, the reading-instant-once loop that already covers quiet, and the new claim-vs-marks assertion), then audit.mjs for palette, contrast against the real composited backdrop, hit targets and leading. The one thing the quiet fixture will NOT exercise afterwards is a strip with a long tail in the quiet composition - keep the full state as the surface that proves the axis derivation still holds for a 41-day job.
